concepts.heading: Understanding Orientation as a Spectrum
concepts.alt: A guide sliding a marker along a long scale with seven notches
concepts.plain: Attraction is a sliding scale. Most people are not 100% one thing.

concepts.heading: The Klein Sexual Orientation Grid
concepts.alt: A guide holding a large grid chart of coloured squares
concepts.plain: Who you are drawn to has many parts, like attraction, feelings and behaviour, and they can differ.

options: The idea that people are either fully straight or fully gay
The idea that people fall in love
checks.explanation: The idea that people are either fully straight or fully gay. In 1948, Dr. Alfred Kinsey published research that challenged the prevailing assumption that people were simply "heterosexual" or "homosexual."

checks.prompt: The Klein Grid shows that orientation is…
options: A constellation of experiences, not one label
checks.explanation: A constellation of experiences, not one label. The Klein Grid reveals something important: sexual orientation is not a single label but a constellation of experiences.

1ff6539f-af94-4a3a-8fb7-10d67b893b14.takeaway: Who you are drawn to sits on a wide range, not in two boxes.

concepts.heading: Beyond Fixed Categories
concepts.alt: A guide holding a flowing ribbon that shifts colour along its length
concepts.plain: For some people, who they are drawn to shifts over the years.

concepts.heading: What Fluidity Is — and Isn't
concepts.alt: A guide standing by a gently flowing stream, a crossed-out light switch beside him
concepts.plain: Shifting is not choosing. You cannot force it or switch it off.

concepts.heading: Fluidity Across Genders
concepts.alt: Four guides standing together inside one flowing wave of colour
concepts.plain: This happens to people of every gender.

concepts.heading: Fluidity and Your Relationships
concepts.plain: A shift in attraction can happen in any relationship. Talk about it.

checks.prompt: Is sexual fluidity the same as choosing your orientation?
options: No, fluidity is not the same as choice
checks.explanation: No, fluidity is not the same as choice. Sexual fluidity is not the same as choice. No one chooses to experience a shift in their attractions any more than they chose their original pattern.

checks.prompt: Later studies found that fluidity exists…
checks.explanation: Across all genders. While Diamond's initial research focused on women, subsequent studies have found that fluidity exists across all genders, though it may manifest differently.

8b4804fc-1690-48ca-83ef-d8d13e86570b.takeaway: Attraction can shift over a lifetime. That is natural, and it is not a choice.

concepts.heading: Understanding Asexuality
concepts.alt: A guide relaxing happily with a book and a slice of cake
concepts.plain: Asexual people feel little or no sexual attraction. It is a real orientation.

concepts.heading: The Split Attraction Model
concepts.alt: A guide holding two separate dials, one marked with a heart and one with a spark
concepts.plain: Romantic pull and sexual pull are two separate things.

concepts.heading: The Aromantic Spectrum
concepts.alt: A guide holding a long colour bar with a small heart at one end that fades out
concepts.plain: Aromantic people feel little or no romantic attraction.

concepts.heading: Ace and Aro People in Relationships
concepts.alt: Two guides sharing a blanket and popcorn on a sofa, laughing as close friends
concepts.plain: Ace and aro people have close, lasting relationships of many kinds.

options: Little or no sexual attraction to others
checks.explanation: Little or no sexual attraction to others. Asexuality is a sexual orientation characterized by a lack of sexual attraction to others, or very low levels of sexual attraction.

checks.prompt: The split attraction model separates which two things?
checks.explanation: Romantic and sexual attraction. One of the most useful frameworks to emerge from ace community discourse is the split attraction model, which separates sexual attraction from romantic attraction.

acebe1d4-1969-431b-b269-50907d46f21a.takeaway: Some people feel little or no sexual or romantic pull, and they still build full, happy relationships.

concepts.heading: Creating Truly Inclusive Spaces
concepts.alt: Four guides standing in an open doorway with arms wide, welcoming
concepts.plain: Knowing the theory matters less than how you treat people.

concepts.heading: Addressing Erasure
concepts.alt: A guide waving to be seen while he fades into a faint outline
concepts.plain: Erasure means acting as if a group, like bi or ace people, is not real.

concepts.heading: Orientation and Relationship Style
concepts.plain: Every orientation shows up in every kind of relationship setup.

concepts.heading: Being an Ally Without Centering Yourself
concepts.alt: She stands just behind him with a supportive hand on his shoulder while he holds the microphone
concepts.plain: Being an ally means listening and backing people up without making it about you.

concepts.heading: When to Seek Support
concepts.plain: If your orientation causes you distress, a supportive therapist can help.

checks.prompt: Treating bisexual people as "really" gay or straight is an example of…
checks.explanation: Erasure. Several forms of orientation erasure persist even in ostensibly progressive communities.

checks.after: Being an Ally Without Centering Yourself
checks.prompt: A core part of genuine allyship is…
checks.explanation: Believing how people identify themselves. Genuine allyship means.

146ec3e3-2de2-41a1-8aeb-9fa6b9a3bda4.takeaway: Believe people about who they are, and treat every orientation as real.
